title: Monitoring AI agents also requires secure review tools
lead: METR reported a test involving the display used to review agent activity.
happened: On October 6, METR published a research note about Inspect, a tool for reviewing the records produced by AI evaluations. A researcher found a problem in the viewer that could cause a reviewer to see a misleading display. The underlying records would remain available. METR said it had not seen agents use this weakness in its evaluations, and the issue was fixed by the tool's developers. The study was conducted in a controlled environment.
matters: Researchers need dependable ways to examine the actions of AI systems. If the interface used for reviewing a test is not reliable, supervisors may misunderstand what happened. This makes the security of evaluation software an important part of responsible AI development.
limits: The study did not document a real agent secretly changing records. It was a controlled demonstration, not evidence that such events are common. More serious future scenarios remain uncertain.
analogy: A recording can be correct even when the screen displaying it is wrong.
